title: Category bar complex and functorial derived colimits
statement:
Let $\mathcal E$ be a small category in the universe of [def-weil-size-convention], endowed with the topology whose covering families are identities, so all presheaves are sheaves [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. For a commutative ring $R$, let $\underline R$ be the constant ring presheaf and $\operatorname{Mod}(\underline R)=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal E^{op},\operatorname{Mod}(R))$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The morphism $\pi_{\mathcal E}^R:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal E),\underline R)\to(*,R)$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism] has inverse image the constant-presheaf functor, identity structural map, and left adjoint $\pi_{\mathcal E,!}^R(F)=\operatorname{colim}_{\mathcal E^{op}}F$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Its total left derived functor $L\pi_{\mathcal E,!}^R:D(\underline R)\to D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] exists, is triangulated, and is left adjoint to the exact constant-presheaf functor. For a module presheaf $F$ in degree zero it is canonically represented by the cochain complex $K_{\mathcal E}(F)$ with
$$K_{\mathcal E}(F)^{-n}=\bigoplus_{U_n\to\cdots\to U_0}F(U_0)\quad(n\geq0),\qquad K_{\mathcal E}(F)^r=0\quad(r>0).$$
Its differential is $\sum_{j=0}^n(-1)^j d_j$: face $d_j$ deletes $U_{n-j}$, composing the adjacent arrows at an internal vertex; if $j<n$ it retains the element of $F(U_0)$, and the last face $d_n$ applies the restriction $F(U_1\to U_0)$. Thus for $n=2$ the differential is $(U_1\to U_0,x)-(U_2\to U_0,x)+(U_2\to U_1,x|_{U_1})$. The functor $K_{\mathcal E}$ takes every objectwise short exact sequence of module presheaves to a degreewise short exact sequence of complexes. For a functor $u:\mathcal E\to\mathcal F$, a ring map $R\to S$, a module presheaf $F$ over $R$ on $\mathcal E$, a module presheaf $G$ over $S$ on $\mathcal F$, and a semilinear natural map $t:F\to u^{-1}G$, the canonical derived-colimit map is represented, after restriction of scalars to $R$, by
$$(U_n\to\cdots\to U_0,x)\longmapsto(uU_n\to\cdots\to uU_0,t_{U_0}(x)).$$
Here $u^{-1}$ is precomposition. These maps preserve identities and composition and commute with the connecting morphisms of short exact sequences. For parallel functors $v,w:\mathcal E\to\mathcal F$, a natural transformation $\eta:v\Rightarrow w$, and $t:F\to w^{-1}G$, the two maps $K(v,G(\eta)t)$ and $K(w,t)$ are chain homotopic and hence equal in $D(R)$. Here $(G(\eta)t)_U=G(\eta_U)t_U$. In particular a natural isomorphism of indexing functors induces the same derived map after the corresponding coefficient identifications.
